summary: Jeffrey L. Broughton works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975 and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University, Long Beach (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Missouri State University and the University of California, Santa Barbara (PhD 2002) under David Gordon White, later becoming an assistant professor at Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Davis Schoening works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox and advisor Sanghasen Singh.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1972) and served as Associate Professor and Director of the Center for South Asian Studies at the University of Virginia (1973–2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1987–1993) and held the J. Newton Rayzor Chair in Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (~2002).
Jeffrey K. Riegel is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He was Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley (1979–2007) and held a post at the University of Sydney (2007–2017).

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University (2015–2016) and a PhD at Leiden University (2017) under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He has held positions at Cornell, Yale, Johns Hopkins, and Boston University, where he became University Professor and Professor of French Literature around 1983.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1964–1970) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of California, Berkeley (1981–1992).

Jeffrey Newmark works in the fields of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (~1992–1996) and the University of British Columbia (~2003–2009), and held a post at the University of Winnipeg (~2010).

Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at Berry College and at the University of Virginia, where he was a visiting assistant professor of religion (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout works in religious studies and philosophy. After earning his PhD from Princeton University (~1972–1976), he served on the faculty at Princeton University as a professor from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Gregory Schopen, and has held teaching posts at UCLA and the University of California, San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006) under the supervision of Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, having previously studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Jens Braarvig works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He has served as a professor at the University of Oslo (2003) and at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (~2003).

Jens Peter Laut is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Klaus Röhrborn in 2008 and held a post at the University of Göttingen from approximately 2008 to 2021.

Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1993–1999) under Josef Simon and became Professor for Theory of Religion at the University of Bern (~2005).

Jens-Uwe Hartmann is an Indologist, Buddhologist, and Tibetologist. He earned his PhD from the University of Munich (~1978–1984), held professorships at the Free University of Berlin and University of Berlin (~1995–2001), and was a professor at Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Kim studied under teachers Rosemary Smith and doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak, completing a PhD at SOAS University of London in 2011.
